entries.subject: ESA/Hubble heic2408a
entries.finding: Little Dumbbell Nebula (M76): g 475, [O III] 502, H-alpha 656, [N II] 658 and I 814 nm; 4000 × 2524 px over 5.01 × 3.16 arcmin. The file's embedded sky tags, used as they are: 0.0751 arcsec per pixel, north 19.1° right of vertical, the frame's centre at 25.5822739°, 51.5752397°. Not measured against Gaia here.

entries.subject: A volume of the Little Dumbbell Nebula
entries.finding: The picture is flat. The Nebula Lab could spread its light in depth where a paper publishes the nebula's three-dimensional shape; that fit has not been made here.
entries.revisitWhen: A published three-dimensional model of the nebula is read and a Nebula Lab recipe is written from it.

entries.subject: Stars in the picture
entries.finding: The photograph first kept its stars, which stood on the nebula's plane whatever their own distances. The Nebula Lab's NOX removes them and keeps the nebula's structure. One pass left the saturated stars, tens of pixels wide; a second pass over a quarter-size copy takes them, and the picture takes that pass's result only where it took a star.
